root_cause.text: The function `nsim_dev_trap_skb_build` allocates an skb and uses `skb_put` to reserve space for an IP header but only partially initializes the `iphdr` struct, leaving multiple fields (e.g., version, ihl, tos, total_length, id, frag_off, ttl, check) uninitialized, causing exposure of uninitialized kernel memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `skb_put(skb, sizeof(struct iphdr))` to `skb_put_zero(skb, sizeof(struct iphdr))` to guarantee zero initialization of the whole IP header, as documented in the commit message: "Fix this by calling skb_put_zero instead of skb_put to guarantee zero initialization of the whole IP header." The CVE description confirms a KMSAN uninit-value originating from `nsim_dev_trap_skb_build`.
